facts.statement: Sthenarosaurus is an extinct genus of rhomaleosaurid pliosauroid found in the Toarcian-aged Main Alum Shale in Whitby, England.
facts.quote: Sthenarosaurus (meaning "strong lizard") is an extinct genus of rhomaleosaurid pliosauroid discovered in the Toarcian-aged 'Main Alum Shale' (Commune subzone of Bifrons zone) in Whitby, England.

facts.statement: The species Sthenarosaurus dawkinsi was named and described in 1909 by D. M. S. Watson.
facts.quote: The type species, Sthenarosaurus dawkinsi, was named and described in 1909 by D. M. S. Watson.

facts.statement: The type specimen for Sthenarosaurus dawkinsi is a set of postcrania discovered in Whitby.
facts.quote: The type specimen is MMUM LL 8023, a set of postcrania discovered in Whitby.

facts.statement: The holotype of Sthenarosaurus consists of an incomplete skeleton lacking a skull.
facts.quote: The holotype is known from an incomplete skeleton with no skull.

facts.statement: Sthenarosaurus is assumed to have been a small plesiosaur reaching up to 3 meters in length when fully grown.
facts.quote: it is assumed that Sthenarosaurus was a small plesiosaur, reaching up to 3 m long when fully grown.

facts.statement: Sthenarosaurus possessed short, thick coracoids and a broad, strong pelvis.
facts.quote: The coracoids were short and thick, while the pelvis was broad and strong.

facts.statement: The dorsal vertebrae of Sthenarosaurus had short but very broad and high centers with thick neural spines.
facts.quote: The dorsal vertebrae possessed short, but very broad and high vertebral centers, with thick neural spines.

facts.statement: Sthenarosaurus has been classified within Pliosauroidea in the order Plesiosauria since its description in 1909.
facts.quote: Sthenarosaurus has been placed in the Pliosauroidea within Plesiosauria since it was described in 1909.

facts.statement: Sthenarosaurus was considered the sister taxon to Archaeonectrus based on similarities in shoulder blade, coracoid, and cervical vertebrae shapes.
facts.quote: It was the sister taxon to Archaeonectrus (known at the time as "Plesiosaurus" rostratus), based on similarities in the shape of the shoulder blades, coracoids and cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Sthenarosaurus might represent an unknown clade of plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: It is possible that Sthenarosaurus represents a currently unknown clade of plesiosaurs.

facts.statement: Sthenarosaurus lived during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 174.7 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Other indeterminate specimens are known, including a pectoral girdle described in 1911.
